config.advertiser_summary: Subscription razors and grooming for men, starting at approximately $5 per month, targeting men who are new to razor subscriptions.

assumptions: subscription: assumed 4.0 orders per customer over ~6 months.
Margin not given; assumed 60% (typical for apparel) for the break-even estimate only.
Break-even per customer (guidance, not enforced): $5 x 60% x 4.0 orders = $12.00.

pricing.rationale: Pay per click: verifiable without trusting a pixel. Maximise conversions within the budget: bids move between $0.25 and the $1.80 cap (category default) to spend it well; no CPA target is invented. Guidance: at the assumed margin, a click is worth about $0.24; bidding above that loses money per customer. Set a target CPA or a lower max CPC to enforce it.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded.

allocations.rationale: score 0.18, relative fit x1.40; 0.0222 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $1.26 (cap $1.80)
score 0.15, relative fit x1.26; 0.0222 conversions/$ at the start, falling as the host saturates; bid $1.14 (cap $1.62)

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: fixed start bid per host; pacing only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded

phases.name: maximize
phases.rule: bid = start x pacing x conversion likelihood, within [floor, cap]: spend the budget on the best opportunities
phases.why: no CPA target was set, so the goal is the most units for the budget

adjustments.reason: Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.
Bid higher when the shopper looks like a likely converter (persona match vs the host's average shopper).

bid_strategy.rationale: Maximise conversions within the budget, never above the $1.80 cap (category default).
